ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; AML/CFT (Definitions) Regulations 2011; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Sanctions Act 2023; Russia Sanctions Act 2022. Beneficial ownership information is collected through customer due diligence and is accessible to the Financial Markets Authority, Inland Revenue Department, New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit, and competent courts; there is no public UBO register in New Zealand.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille Convention destination: notarized certificate or certified extract -> Apostille issued by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. For a non-Apostille destination: notarized certificate or certified extract -> consular legalization by the destination jurisdiction's embassy or consulate in New Zealand. These two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille and consular legalization on the same document.

For a Hague Apostille Convention destination: notarized certificate -> Apostille issued by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. For a non-Apostille destination: notarized certificate -> consular legalization by the destination jurisdiction's consulate or embassy in New Zealand. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never apply both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the New Zealand company, notarized by a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille Convention destination: notarized executed resolution -> Apostille by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. For a non-Apostille destination: notarized executed resolution -> consular legalization at the destination jurisdiction's consulate in New Zealand. Use one route exclusively; do not chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (certified copy of registered constitution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille Convention destination: notarized certified copy -> Apostille by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. For a non-Apostille destination: notarized certified copy -> consular legalization by the destination jurisdiction's diplomatic mission in New Zealand. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never use them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed New Zealand bank issuing on official bank letterhead
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille Convention destination: notarized bank letter -> Apostille by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. For a non-Apostille destination: notarized bank letter -> consular legalization by the destination jurisdiction's embassy or consulate in New Zealand. Use only one of the two authentication paths; do not chain them.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening must cover all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, senior management, commercial counterparties, intermediaries, and payment beneficiaries against (i) New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit lists and Financial Markets Authority enforcement actions; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list; (iii) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) HM Treasury consolidated sanctions list; (v) EU global human rights and terrorism sanctions; (vi) New Zealand autonomous sanctions under the Sanctions Act 2023 and Russia Sanctions Act 2022. The screening program must include near-match resolution for aliases, PEP determination, negative-news checks, source-of-wealth verification, risk-tiered due diligence, and immediate suspicious transaction reporting to the NZ Police FIU within statutory timeframes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register online name clearance portal (MBIE); NZBN nzbn.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory company names must be in Latin/Roman script; Chinese characters are not accepted on the New Zealand register. Use an English-language distinctive element, and if a Chinese trade name is desired it may be used separately on invoices or marketing but not as the legal name. The four-tier naming test requires: (1) legal suffix Limited or Ltd; (2) name not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name; (3) no prohibited or sensitive token without prior ministerial, regulator, or relevant Crown authorization; (4) no misleading, offensive, objectionable, or prohibited content.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the applicant must first study the Registrar's stated grounds. There is no formal extension for a name reservation; the current reservation expires after the applicable window and a new reservation application may be filed while the name remains available. The applicant may submit a written administrative review to the New Zealand Companies Office Registrar within 20 working days of rejection, including the original rejection notice, supporting evidence, any written consents from affected holders, and a statutory argument. If the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may file an application for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand. Resubmitting the identical rejected name without new evidence or consent is ineffective.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Companies Act 1993, a registered office must be a physical location in New Zealand, and a reputable virtual office service may satisfy this only if it provides a real street address, physical inspection access, and reliable mail handling. However, for a wholesale distributor of optical frames, the Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand banks will generally reject a pure virtual mailbox or commercial mailbox as the company's place of business for GST registration, bank account opening, and commercial substance review. The company should secure a serviced office or leased physical workspace under the company's name, maintain staff or operational management at the address, and preserve records there to meet tax and AML/CFT expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is low, approximately 10-15%, for a properly registered low-risk wholesale trader maintaining clean records and a physical office. Checklist: (1) registered office is accessible and not a PO Box; (2) company name plate or signage is visible; (3) statutory records and GST/tax filings are current; (4) directors' addresses and service addresses are consistent; (5) no unlicensed or financial-product activities are present; (6) bank account and payment platforms are used only for legitimate wholesale transactions. Unannounced physical inspections by the Inland Revenue Department or Companies Office are uncommon but may occur on GST audits, AML/CFT supervision, complaint-led inquiries, or insolvency risk assessments; use of a virtual office raises this risk materially.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 2020), in particular sections 10, 11, 12, 16, 21, 22, 31, 35, 42, 122, 126, 151, 161, 180, 189, 190, 191, 200 and 208; Financial Reporting Act 2013; Companies (Fees) Regulations 2016.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); online registry at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company submitted under section 10 of the Companies Act 1993 through the Companies Office online system, which upon approval issues the Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand company law does not impose a minimum paid-up share capital requirement for an ordinary limited company. The company must have at least one share, but there is no statutory escrow account or blocked capital deposit. Shares may be issued fully paid, partly paid, or credited as paid for lawful non-cash consideration in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the company's constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FORMAL PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF NZ LTD (the Company), EFFECTIVE AS AT [DATE]. The directors of the Company, in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Company's constitution, convened the first board meeting and, a quorum being present, unanimously adopted the following resolutions: (1) Share Capital Subscription and Allotment. That the allotment of ordinary shares to the subscribers in the amounts recorded in the Company's register of shareholders be ratified, confirmed and accepted; such shares are issued fully paid or credited as paid pursuant to the constitution; the directors and officers are authorised to execute share subscription agreements, issue physical or electronic share certificates, and note all ownership, transfer, entitlement and forfeiture entries in the shareholder register. (2) Registered Office and Principal Place of Business. That the registered office of the Company be fixed at [address], New Zealand, and the principal place of business at [business address]; the Board authorises the filing of the registered office and any subsequent changes with the Registrar of Companies; the registered office shall be open during ordinary business hours for service of documents and notices. (3) Adoption of Constitution and Governance Instruments. That the constitution presented to the Board, a copy of which has been entered into the registered records, is approved; directors shall act in accordance with the Companies Act 1993, the constitution, and any shareholder agreement; corporate records, registers and minutes shall be maintained at the registered office or an authorised location. (4) Corporate Banking and Signatory Mandate. That the Company shall open current, foreign currency and platform-payment business accounts with [Bank] in New Zealand; the Board appoints [Signatory A], [Signatory B] and [Signatory C] as authorised signatories, with any payment or transfer exceeding NZD [*] requiring two signatories; the mandate includes SWIFT telegraphic transfer and platform payment rails; banking forms and operating agreements are approved and the officers are directed to complete AML/CFT due diligence with the bank. (5) Appointment of Statutory and Executive Officers. That [Director 1] is appointed as Managing Director, [Director 2] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary if such office is established, each with authority to sign, lodge and receive statutory returns, convene shareholder meetings and procure compliance. (6) Tax and Employer Registration. That applications be made to Inland Revenue for an IRD number, GST registration, PAYE/employer registration and any non-resident withholding tax or customs client code; the Board approves the engagement of registered tax agents and authorises electronic lodgement through Inland Revenue's MyIR service. (7) Common Seal and Execution of Instruments. That the Company may adopt or dispense with a common seal; without a common seal, contracts are validly executed in accordance with section 180 of the Companies Act 1993 by two directors, or one director and one officer, or other means approved by the Board. (8) Ratification and General Authority. That all steps taken by subscribers and incorporators to reserve the name, incorporate the Company, obtain the New Zealand Business Number and appoint initial directors are ratified; any director or officer is authorised to execute all collateral documents necessary to give full legal effect to the above resolutions. This resolution constitutes a single and complete governance mandate and shall be entered into the Board minutes. Certified copies may be relied upon by banks, government agencies and commercial counterparties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Registered Office Confirmation and Pre-Incorporation Governance Pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / MBIE Business Registration Service at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the Companies Register for exact name and intellectual similarity, confirm no usage of prohibited expressions under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993, and verify that the proposed name contains a legal suffix such as Limited or Ltd. Prepare the governance pack by identifying at least one New Zealand-resident director, at least one shareholder, the number of shares to be subscribed, the registered office physical address, and the constitution to be adopted or the statutory default terms. Obtain signed director consents and shareholder authorities. For wholesale distribution of eyewear frames, no separate pre-incorporation licence is required, but zoning of the proposed business address should be confirmed with the local council.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternative names
Date and place of incorporation instruction
Shareholder names, share allocations and beneficial ownership declaration
Director names, residential addresses, dates of birth, nationality and consent forms
Registered office physical address and occupant consent
Authority from beneficial owner if different from subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, file a written request for consent from the existing name holder, add distinguishing words, or submit a new name; if a director is ineligible or fails the disqualification check, replace that director before incorporation and resubmit the application; any delay is tracked by the Companies Office query queue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Filing and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies via Companies Office online incorporation; New Zealand Business Number Program, MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the authorised Companies Office portal, select the company incorporation service, input the reserved name and Part 1 information, attach the director consents and constitution, set the registered office and address for service, complete the shareholding structure, and submit the application electronically. Pay the non-refundable registration fee by credit or debit card or online banking using the official fee schedule. The Registrar will examine the application for compliance and, if satisfied, register the company and issue the Certificate of Incorporation with a company number and NZBN simultaneously. Confirm the submitted date, print the certificate and keep the electronic pack in the corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of deficiency or suspends the application, file a corrective response through the online case dashboard, pay any shortfall if the fee declined, or withdraw and resubmit; if the company was accidentally registered, an application for removal from the register may be made under section 328 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Corporate Governance Books and Bank Account Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; New Zealand bank under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate is issued, convene the first board meeting in person or by electronic means, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, approve the share issue and issue share certificates. Open the company's statutory registers including the shareholder register, director register, register of charges and records of directors' interests. Execute the corporate bank agreement and present the bank with the resolution, certificate of incorporation and directors' identification; the bank will perform AML/CFT customer due diligence, beneficial ownership verification, and then activate SWIFT and platform payment rails. Obtain and place in the minute book a certified copy of the banking mandate.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT identity documents and beneficial ownership declaration
Bank forms, account mandate and signatory proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank declines to open an account or imposes enhanced due diligence, provide certified translated corporate documents, a consolidated group structure chart and source-of-funds evidence; if the board is deadlocked, a written resolution may be signed by all directors or shareholders may appoint an additional director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Tax Registration, GST/PAYE and Cross-Border Trade Credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department via MyIR; New Zealand Customs Service; Accident Compensation Corporation if employing staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company using the NZBN on Inland Revenue's business registration service, obtain an income tax IRD number, register for GST if annual taxable turnover is or will exceed NZD 60,000, register for PAYE and KiwiSaver if employees will be engaged, and apply for a Customs client code for future import or export of acetate eyewear frames. If the company purchases from overseas, set up import transaction records and a duty deferment account if required. For low-risk optical frame distribution, no special excise licence applies, but all invoices, packing slips and commercial documents must include the NZBN, GST number and supplier details to satisfy consumer information rules.
required_dossiers: Bank account details for GST refunds
Customs client code form and import/export plans
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue flags a tax mismatch or the company misses the automatic registration trigger, apply for late registration and seek tax clearance; if Customs rejects the client code application, provide supplier invoices and HS commodity classification. Past filing errors may be corrected via voluntary disclosure with no penalty if made promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Premises Occupancy, Workplace Health and Safety and Distribution-Only Licensing Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial local authority (district or city council); WorkSafe New Zealand; Fire and Emergency New Zealand as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the leased or owned premises is zoned for wholesale, showroom and storage under the district plan, and obtain any building occupancy certificate or building warrant of fitness if the building contains specified systems such as a fire alarm or sprinkler. Carry out a health and safety risk assessment under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and record the due diligence. Because ISIC 4646 is wholesale distribution only, no Environmental Impact Assessment or manufacturing discharge licence is required. If a warehouse is operated with no processing, confirm no HSNO chemicals are stored, and keep fire escape routes and extinguishers certified.
required_dossiers: Building Warrant of Fitness or occupancy certificate if applicable
Fire safety and evacuation plan with FENZ records
Health and Safety at Work risk register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the council issues a notice of unauthorised land use or building non-compliance, cease the non-complying activity and submit a resource consent or building consent application; if FENZ identifies fire risk, install required systems within the notice period. The company may operate from an alternative address during remediation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; local territorial authority and WorkSafe New Zealand have residual jurisdiction for building occupancy and workplace safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable for ISIC 4646 wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames; any physical premises used as an office, showroom or warehouse remains subject to building occupancy, fire evacuation and occupational safety approvals.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (New Zealand) and territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No Environmental Impact Assessment required for wholesale distribution of acetate eyewear frames; no manufacturing, processing, discharge or hazardous waste generation. If future warehousing exceeds RMA land-use thresholds, an Assessment of Environmental Effects under section 88 of the RMA may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. No industrial wastewater, VOC emissions or hazardous waste streams are generated by wholesale, display and storage; any general municipal solid waste must be collected by an authorised waste contractor and disposed of in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008. If future coating, surfacing or lens fabrication is added, the activity would be reassessed as manufacturing and would require an AEE and potentially a discharge permit under section 15 of the RMA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as a civil-defence facility. For any occupied premises, a Building Act 2004 Building Warrant of Fitness may be required where the building has specified systems such as fire alarms or sprinklers; Fire and Emergency New Zealand operates fire safety and evacuation requirements under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; employers must carry out a risk assessment under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and comply with WorkSafe New Zealand guidance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - New Zealand; online portal: myIR at www.ird.govt.nz. The IRD number is the sole TIN and GST/VAT identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: For an NZ-limited company, incorporate or register with the New Zealand Companies Office under the Companies Act 1993. A foreign non-resident entity not already registered must first register as an overseas company under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993. Step 2: Obtain or confirm the IRD number, normally triggered by Companies Office integration, or apply to Inland Revenue through myIR for a non-resident company or overseas company; a New Zealand address for service or New Zealand tax agent may be required. Step 3: Register for GST in myIR using the same IRD number; there is no separate GST/VAT registration number. Registration is compulsory once taxable supplies exceed the statutory threshold, but voluntary registration is available for exporters to substantiate zero-rating and recover input tax. Step 4: Preserve the IRD confirmation, Companies Office registration details, and myIR account credentials for all tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None in the US check-the-box sense. A qualifying close-held New Zealand company may elect into the Look-Through Company (LTC) regime under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, but this election is not assumed and is separate from the standard default entity-level taxation. GST grouping elections are available under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Hybrid mismatch rules apply mandatorily under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018; no elective hybrid-mismatch relief exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - value-added consumption tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months or expected to be exceeded in the next 12 months; remote services supplied by non-resident suppliers to New Zealand consumers are captured at the same NZD 60,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API pre-clearance regime exists in New Zealand. Tax invoices must contain the prescribed particulars under section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Voluntary PEPPOL e-invoicing is available through the New Zealand e-Invoicing network. Inland Revenue accepts electronic records; GST records must be retained for seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, a supply of goods is zero-rated when the supplier exports the goods or supplies them in the course of export and the goods physically leave New Zealand within 28 days of supply; for this international wholesale optical frames business, the exporter must demonstrate delivery to a non-resident overseas customer and physical departure from New Zealand. Services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and the services are not in connection with New Zealand land or goods and are not consumed in New Zealand. Remote and digital services supplied to New Zealand resident consumers are standard-rated at 15% under section 11A and are not eligible for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs electronic export declaration, lodged through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window under the Customs and Excise Act 2018, showing the optical goods, quantity, value, export date and overseas consignee
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight issued by the carrier and evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and packing list cross-referenced to the customs declaration and the wholesale optical frames contract

Foreign exchange repatriation evidence: bank SWIFT credit advice, telegraphic transfer advice, or account statement showing settlement of export proceeds into the New Zealand exporter's account, functioning as the New Zealand equivalent of an inward remittance certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the 0% GST rate is claimed without verified export documentation, Inland Revenue may recharacterise the supply as standard-rated, assess 15% GST, and charge use-of-money interest from the original filing date. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, shortfall penalties apply at 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for an abusive tax position, and 100% for evasion or similar acts. False or knowingly incorrect export documents can trigger criminal prosecution under the Crimes Act 1961 and the Tax Administration Act 1994. If goods are diverted back into the New Zealand market, or export proceeds are not repatriated within the expected 180-day window, the zero-rating may be clawed back retrospectively and the full GST amount plus penalties becomes immediately due.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a freely convertible currency regime under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. There is no central bank-administered exchange control, no surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no limitation on current account transactions. Capital account convertibility is also unrestricted for ordinary cross-border equity and debt flows, provided the Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent thresholds are not engaged; for this wholesale optical frames distribution entity, no OIO consent is triggered unless the investment targets sensitive land, fishing quota, or significant business assets, which is not the case here. Profit remittances may be made freely in NZD or any convertible currency via licensed registered banks. The only barriers are standard tax compliance duties such as New Zealand IRD registration, non-resident withholding tax on dividends or interest if applicable, and AML/CFT source-of-funds diligence. The NZD has no dual rate, no rationing, and no administrative pre-approval for foreign exchange transactions. Accordingly, liquidity can be managed openly with no need for parallel-market buffers, though prudent treasury policy should still document economic substance and arm's-length pricing to protect treaty and transfer-pricing positions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory foreign exchange surrender requirement for export receipts in New Zealand. Exporters may retain 100% of foreign currency earnings in licensed bank accounts, settle them into NZD at any time, or use them directly for cross-border payments. No regulator-imposed conversion timeline or mandatory ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account plus NZD Foreign Currency Settlement Sub-Account
Basic Operational Currency Account plus NZD Foreign Currency Settlement Sub-Account
Basic Operational Currency Account plus NZD Foreign Currency Settlement Sub-Account
Basic Operational Currency Account plus NZD Foreign Currency Settlement Sub-Account
Basic Operational Currency Account only for lower-volume treasury flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury clearing rail. New Zealand law does not formally classify EMI-style payment companies as 'banks' under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989, and none of the licensed non-bank payment providers hold direct settlement account membership in the Exchange Settlement Account System operated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. A fintech EMI could only provide pre-funded, pass-through payment initiation services, not genuine bank-grade clearing or FX settlement. Therefore, it cannot replace a Tier-1 registered commercial bank for statutory tax verification, capital verification, trade finance instruments, or direct SWIFT clearing. Use of an EMI is acceptable only as a supplementary wallet for low-value Platform_Pay transactions, subject to strict pre-screening and ECB-style e-money limits adapted to NZ AML/CFT rules; it must not be used for capital injection, dividend repatriation, or documentary trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand has no statutory mandate requiring directors to appear physically in-branch for account opening. Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, banks may rely on remote electronic identity verification using Biometric Document Verification, Credential Authentication, and video-linked interviews. For this low-risk wholesale distribution entity, major banks typically allow a remote on-boarding process where the director provides a notarised identity pack, live video confirmation, and an IRD-completed Entity/Organisation Information form. A New Zealand registered office address and a local appointed Director or Authorised Agent are nevertheless strongly recommended. Some banks reserve the right to request physical presence for foreign directors whose documentation cannot be verified electronically, but a consular-legalised proxy opening is generally accepted provided the bank's Compliance Committee approves the source-of-funds narrative. All directors must still be identifiable through the New Zealand Companies Office register, and ultimate beneficial ownership must be disclosed to 25% or greater thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained beneficial ownership chain with non-resident individual shareholders or family trusts hiding behind nominee directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organisation chart signed by directors; Certificate of Incorporation and Constitution from the New Zealand Companies Office; Registry extracts for all intermediate holding companies; notarised passports and proof of residential address for every natural person with 25% or more ownership; trust deed, trustee register, and written confirmation of source of initial trust funds if a corporate trustee is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection via private transfer from a high-risk jurisdiction or uncorroborated personal wealth, creating source-of-funds ambiguity for capital verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements for the originating account covering a 12-month period; signed and audited financial statements or a contemporaneous management account pack for the funding company; foreign tax return evidence matching the sent amounts; notarised share subscription agreement and board resolution from the NZ_LTD company authorising receipt; default-generated wire confirmation referencing the share subscription purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade counterparty and buyer/seller screening red flags, particularly where optical eyewear frames are procured from jurisdictions with perceived high money-laundering or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KYC pack for each material supplier and buyer including sanctions screening results, corporate registry extracts, and ultimate beneficial ownership declarations; purchase orders, pro-forma invoices, and transport documents (bill of lading or airway bill) evidencing genuine trade flows; 3-way matching to be maintained for goods, payment, and invoice; a written transaction rationale memorandum describing the goods, pricing method, and inventory flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency and economic-substance ambiguity causing the bank to view NZ_LTD as a potential shell vehicle rather than a genuine wholesaler
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NZ IRD tax number and Resident Withholding Tax certificate; lease or sub-lease agreement for a physical storage/office footprint in New Zealand; employment records or service agreement for local operational staff; bank-verified flow of operational expenditure (rent, salaries, utilities) in New Zealand; current tax compliance report or tax agent letter confirming no outstanding tax liabilities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent's Tier-1 commercial bank to the NZ_LTD operating account at a registered bank, using the BPM6/IMF Balance of Payments code for Direct Investment - Equity Capital. The purpose of remittance field must state 'Share Capital Subscription' or 'Capital Contribution for Wholesale Optical Frames Business'. The inward remittance direction should be documented by the sending bank's source-of-funds confirmation, the NZ receiving bank's remittance receipt, and the Companies Office share allotment filing. After receipt, the bank will conduct capital verification against the signed board resolution, shareholder loan agreement (if applicable), and audited financial statement. No RBNZ pre-approval is required because New Zealand has no exchange-control gate; however, if the shareholder is non-resident, the NZ entity must file an IRD disclosure and confirm no OIO consent requirement via a statutory declaration. For any convertible loan, a formal loan agreement and interest rate schedule should avoid hidden equity treatment by the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for importing acetate frames and exporting finished eyewear should use standard clearing rails: for open account supplier payments, SWIFT MT103 with full invoice and shipping evidence filed for auditing; for documentary risk mitigation, a commercial Letter of Credit opened through the NZ bank as issuing bank and delivered via SWIFT MT700 to the beneficiary bank; for payment-on-documentation, Documentary Collections via MT400/MT412 with transport documents endorsed to the collecting bank. All MT103s must include the correct BIC, account number, and IRD payment reference if applicable. Resident Withholding Tax on interest and Non-Resident Contractors Withholding Tax for overseas suppliers must be checked. Since the entity operates in NZD but trades globally, the treasury should maintain multi-currency accounts and pre-agreed swing lines with the local clearing bank to avoid excessive FX conversion costs on simultaneous inbound and outbound flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD/USD forward contracts and forward swaps of up to 12 months tenor
Deliverable NZD/EUR and NZD/CNH forwards for corridor purchases from Asia
Cross-currency swaps between NZD and USD or EUR for effective converted funding cost management
FX options on deliverable NZD pairs, including vanilla European-style options for protective floors and caps
Synthetic forwards using swap combinations on the over-the-counter interbank market, with ISDA and CSA documentation applied
Offsetting forward contracts with foreign exchange netting under a local master agreement with the banking institution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Company (Companies Act 1993, section 208)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the Annual Return Date, which is the last day of the month in which the anniversary of registration falls; for example, a 15 July incorporation has an Annual Return Date of 31 July and a filing deadline of 31 August.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Registrar may issue a compliance reminder and final notice; if the annual return remains unfiled for two consecutive annual return dates, the Registrar may initiate administrative removal/strike-off from the New Zealand Companies Register after prior notice. On strike-off the company ceases to exist as a legal person and its assets may vest in the Crown. Directors may also be prosecuted for failure to ensure the annual return is filed, with fines up to NZ$10,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Income Tax Return (IR4) and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand Government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, a company that does not use a tax agent must file and pay by 7 July following balance date; registered tax agent extensions may apply under IRD rules. Provisional tax instalments must also be paid on the prescribed dates if the company has residual income tax above the provisional tax threshold.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$50 for each month or part-month the return is overdue, capped at NZ$500 for most returns; use-of-money interest on unpaid tax at the IRD prescribed underpayment rate, currently 10.70% per annum; late payment penalties; persistent default can trigger IRD enforcement action including company liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements and annual report to shareholders, including auditor's report where a statutory audit is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the company; where the company is an FMC reporting entity or otherwise required by law, filed with the Companies Office or Financial Markets Authority as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the company's balance date; for a 31 March balance date, the financial statements must be prepared and made available by 31 August.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice, or to deliver them to shareholders, may be subject to enforcement by the Registrar; failure to appoint an auditor when legally required is an offence under the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013, with fines on conviction and court-ordered compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax (GST) returns and payment, if the company is registered for GST
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand Government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The 28th day after the end of each taxable period; filing frequency may be monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly as elected at registration. For a six-monthly filer with periods ending 31 March and 30 September, returns are due by 28 April and 28 October respectively.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties, late payment penalties, and use-of-money interest at the IRD prescribed rate, currently 10.70% per annum, apply; IRD may issue an assessment and pursue enforcement through garnishee, bankruptcy, or liquidation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit by a licensed chartered accountant/CPA auditor is mandatory if: (1) the company is large under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, meaning in each of the two immediately preceding accounting periods it has total assets exceeding NZ$60 million, or total revenue exceeding NZ$30 million, or 50 or more full-time equivalent employees; (2) the company is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, such as a listed issuer or registered managed investment scheme; (3) shareholders holding not less than 5% of the voting rights validly request an audit; or (4) the company's constitution, shareholder resolution, or board resolution requires an audit. A non-large, non-FMC private company is otherwise exempt from a mandatory statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand accounting standards issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB): full NZ IFRS for Tier 1 public accountability entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) for eligible Tier 2 for-profit entities; and the XRB simpler reporting framework for small for-profit entities not publicly accountable. Financial statements must comply with the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013, while tax filings follow the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Tax Administration Act 1994.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand requires every company to maintain and hold a Register of Significant Controllers (RSC) at its registered office. A significant controller is any individual who, directly or indirectly, owns or controls more than 25% of the ordinary shares or voting rights, has the right to appoint or remove a majority of directors, or is otherwise able to exercise significant control. The RSC must be updated within 10 working days of the company becoming aware of any change in significant control, not merely at the annual return date. Share transfers must be registered in the Register of Members within 30 days of lodgement; if the transfer alters significant control, the RSC must also be updated within the applicable 10-working-day window. The annual return filed with the Companies Office serves as the annual confirmation step, and directors must confirm the RSC information is complete and accurate as at the annual return date. Failure to establish, maintain, or update the RSC is an offence under the Companies (Disclosure of Involved Persons) Amendment Act 2022, with fines for the company and every officer in default.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of board meetings, shareholder meetings, and resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 900 per year for a compliant New Zealand registered office and corporate secretarial agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 18,000 per year for a standard New Zealand private wholesale company engaged in international distribution, depending on transaction volume, complexity, and whether the audit is performed under full NZ IFRS or NZ IFRS RDR

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax incentive (15% credit on eligible R&D expenditure); no free-zone regime, patent box, or preferential holding-company exemption; imputation credit system provides deferral only to resident shareholders.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (subject to shareholder continuity of at least 49% or business continuity test under s IA 5 Income Tax Act 2007)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Corporate Income Tax Return filed electronically through Inland Revenue myIR portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July. With a tax agent extension, filing may be deferred to 31 March of the following year. For non-standard balance dates, the due date is the 7th day of the second month after the balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal income – gross income from trading activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare total gross revenue from the wholesale international distribution of acetate eyeglass frames. A non-resident company must report only New Zealand-sourced income derived through its NZ fixed establishment; foreign-source agency and distribution income is outside the NZ tax net unless the non-resident has a permanent establishment in NZ. Where related-party sales are made to associated distributors, prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and include a reconciliation in the notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, dividends, and other investment income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all interest, dividend, and other passive income received. For a non-resident limited company, any embedded NRWT credits on cross-border payments must be shown; claim DTA-protected lower rates only when a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration are appended.

Sum of Box 1 and Box 2. Confirm that no amount was double-counted via a CFC or branch-equivalent attribution. A non-resident that is tax resident in NZ is taxable on worldwide income; otherwise only NZ-source amounts are included.

List all deductible costs including cost of goods sold, freight, warehousing, logistics, royalties, management fees, and operating overheads. Cross-border payments to associated foreign group companies must satisfy the arm's length standard; expenses that are not incurred in producing assessable income (e.g., capital outlays, fines, 50% of entertainment expenditure) are disallowed. For a non-resident head office, NZ branch expense apportionment must be documented under the OECD authorised OECD approach.

Calculate Box 3 minus Box 4. If the result is a loss, enter nil income tax; adjust for any tax timing differences and non-deductible items. Ensure that transfer pricing corrections are made before the return is filed.

Claim available net tax losses under the ownership continuity rules (49% continuity of beneficial ownership) or the business continuity test. A loss from the period before a 51% ownership change is forfeited unless the company continues the same or similar business with the same core assets; document the shareholder register for non-resident owners to demonstrate continuity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits and withholding tax credits (RWT/NRWT)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record domestic imputation credits attached to resident dividends and any RWT/NRWT credits. Non-resident shareholders are not entitled to imputation credits on distributions; instead, the paying company must deduct NRWT when declaring a dividend. Attach the IR67 withholding tax reconciliation showing NRWT paid on all outgoing distributions.

Apply the 28% statutory company rate to taxable income, apply credits from Box 7, and compute the residual tax due. Provisional tax instalments made via myIR are credited against this amount; late payment interest runs on any shortfall. If claiming a reduced DTA withholding on outgoing payments, verify that the beneficial ownership certificate was in the payer's file at payment date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 per month or part-month for an overdue IR4, together with late payment interest at the Inland Revenue prescribed rate on unpaid tax. A false return or tax evasion triggers a shortfall penalty up to 150% of the tax avoided, and criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994 s 143A may result in a fine up to NZ$50,000 and up to 5 years' imprisonment for officers and directors involved in the fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid to non-residents, subject to DTA reductions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower treaty rate, the NZ payer must obtain, before payment, a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the recipient's jurisdiction, plus a written beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient is the true owner of the dividend income and not a conduit or nominee. The payer then files an IR67 return and remits NRWT at the reduced treaty rate. If over-withheld, the non-resident may file an IR3NR refund application within the statutory four-year period, attaching the TRC, dividend vouchers, and a completed certificate of tax residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest NRWT is 15%; most NZ DTAs reduce the rate to 10%. Statutory royalty NRWT is 15%; OECD-pattern DTAs generally reduce the rate to 10% (or 5% for certain copyright royalties). Where income is attributable to a permanent establishment, NRWT does not apply and the amount is taxed as business profits at 28%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZ$1,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in a tax year; the Inland Revenue may request documentation for lower value transactions where significant transfer pricing risk is identified.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not impose a UAE-style ESR regime, but the doctrine of economic substance is entrenched in: (1) tax residence requiring the company's centre of effective management to be in NZ; (2) treaty entitlement requiring the recipient to be the beneficial owner of the income; and (3) the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG1 Income Tax Act 2007) which recharacterises shell structures lacking commercial substance. A mail-box entity or conduit used to access treaty benefits without real activity will be denied relief and the income will be re-attributed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting New Zealand-sourced wholesale revenues from the IR4, or inflating intercompany purchase invoices from a related overseas optical frame supplier to reduce taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 1994 s 141: shortfall penalty of 150% of the tax avoided; s 143A criminal offence: fine of up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years. The company is also liable for unpaid tax plus arrears interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign or cause the filing of a false return are subject to civil asset recovery for the entire tax lost, a personal penalty up to 150% of the evaded tax, disqualification from managing companies under the Companies Act 1993, and criminal imprisonment for up to 5 years on conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying supra-normal royalties or management fees to a related tax-haven entity that has no developers, employees, or assets, with no credible transfer pricing analysis and no economic substance supporting the payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 s GC 13 (transfer pricing adjustment) and s GC 6 (reconstruction); shortfall penalty under TAA s 141 up to 150% if the adjustment is not a reasonably arguable position; interest on unpaid tax from the due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or implement the sham arrangement may be personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties, ordered to pay equitable compensation to the company for breach of fiduciary duty, subjected to a travel ban (border alert) while tax debts are outstanding, and criminally prosecuted for evasion if the arrangement involved deliberate concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: DTA Treaty Abuse – Beneficial Ownership Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividend or royalty payments through a low-tax intermediary without any real business or substance, then claiming treaty relief on the basis of false Tax Residency Certificates or incorrect beneficial ownership declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: General anti-avoidance rule (s BG1) invalidates the tax advantage; the anti-treaty-shopping limitation in the relevant DTA denies relief; NRWT at 30% (dividends) or 15% (royalty) becomes immediately payable; shortfall penalty under TAA s 141 of 100% – 150% of the avoided tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the beneficial ownership declaration knowing it to be false are personally criminally liable under TAA s 143(1)(c) and s 143A, carrying a maximum of 5 years' imprisonment and a NZ$50,000 fine. Civil liability includes restitution of all underpaid withholding taxes and indemnification of the company against penalties, with worldwide asset tracing available to the Inland Revenue.
